steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Reasoning:**  
September 30, 2026 at 17:00 ET (UTC-4) converts to 23:00 CEST (UTC+2) on the same day in Madrid.

**ANSWER:** 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Peru uses PET (UTC-5) year-round with no DST.  
July 15, 2026 12:00 UTC is therefore 07:00 the same day in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Japan Standard Time (JST) is UTC+9, while CEST is UTC+2, so the deadline is 7 hours ahead in Tokyo.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The contest deadline is October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT (UTC-7). Madrid uses CEST (UTC+2) in October, which is a 9-hour difference ahead of PDT. Adding 9 hours to 23:59 on Oct 11 gives 08:59 on Oct 12.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is in the CET/CEST time zone. On March 3, 2026, Spain will be observing CET (UTC+1), as DST starts later in March. PST is UTC-8, so the difference is exactly 9 hours.

March 3, 2026, 23:59 PST converts to March 4, 2026, 08:59 CET.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is UTC+1 (no DST in February). Los Angeles is PST (UTC-8) in February. The time difference is 9 hours (LA is behind).

10:00 CET on Feb 2 = 01:00 PST on Feb 2.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Peru uses PET (UTC-5) year-round with no DST. JST is UTC+9, a 14-hour difference (JST is ahead).  
8:00 AM JST on 2026-05-05 is 18:00 on the previous day in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT is 2026-10-29 07:59 in Madrid (CEST, UTC+2).

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET is 14:00 in Madrid (CET, UTC+1, no DST in late October).

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM Pacific Time (PT, which is UTC-7 in 2026 as daylight saving ends on Nov 1). Madrid uses Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) with no DST in early November, resulting in an 8-hour difference.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT is 2026-03-21 07:59 in Madrid (CET, UTC+1).  
ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

March 25, 2026, 12:00 CET is 03:00 PDT on the same day (Los Angeles is 9 hours behind CET in late March, after the DST switch).

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 03:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Reasoning:**  
October 12, 2026 at 12:00 AM ET is the same as 2026-10-12 04:00 UTC (midnight ET = 5 hours behind UTC). Madrid uses Central European Time (CET). In October 2026, Spain is on standard time (CET, UTC+1), not daylight saving time. Adding 1 hour to UTC gives 05:00 local time on the same day.

**ANSWER:** 2026-10-12 05:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is in the CEST time zone (UTC+2). AoE is UTC-12, so the deadline is 23:59 on 2026-10-09 in UTC-12, which converts to 2026-10-10 11:59 in UTC, and then to 2026-10-10 13:59 in CEST.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Reasoning:**  
PT is UTC-7 (no DST in August 2026 for Pacific Time). Madrid uses CEST (UTC+2) in August. The difference is 9 hours ahead.  
12:00 PM PT on 2026-08-14 converts to 21:00 local time on the same day.

**ANSWER:** 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

IST is UTC+5:30. Madrid (CET/CEST) in November 2026 will be on CET (UTC+1), as DST ends on the last Sunday of October.

Converting 23:59 IST on 2026-11-10: subtract 4 hours 30 minutes to reach 19:29 CET on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Nepal Time (NPT) is UTC+5:45. Peru (Lima) is UTC-5, so the difference is exactly 10 hours and 45 minutes (Peru is behind).  
5:00 PM NPT on 2026-04-02 is 06:15 on the same calendar day in Lima time.

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Adelaide is in ACST (UTC+9:30). Madrid is in CEST (UTC+2) on that date in 2026. The difference is 7.5 hours (Adelaide is ahead).  
10:00 ACST on 2026-10-06 is 02:30 CEST on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 02:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney is AEDT (UTC+11) on October 3 2026.  
Madrid is CEST (UTC+2).  
Difference: 9 hours earlier in Madrid.  
6:00 PM Sydney = 09:00 same day in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 09:00
